newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank to create new credit card jobs.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank to create new credit card jobs.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland officially opened new premises for its Credit Card Centre in Southend on Thursday and said it expected to create over 200 new jobs in the next five years.
The Royal Bank's Credit Card Centre first opened in Southend, South-East England in 1972, employing just 12 people. In the last four years the number employed has risen by 150 to 450.
Southend processes credit card transactions and payments for the Royal bank and RBS Advanta, the bank's joint venture with U.S. card issuer Advanta Corporation.
"The Credit card business has grown rapidly over the last 25 years," said the Royal Bank's Director Card Services, Andrew Waldman.
"In 1972 the Royal Bank had just over 140,000 credit cards on issue, while today the figure is more than one million and we process almost 35 million credit card transactions a year."
Last year the bank's credit card lending increased by 72 percent to 748 million stg.
